text: Read the operator's linked repository, mayhem82/bellbrook-advocacy-flying-fox-form, for context before any case material was supplied: a standalone resident impact-record form (local storage only, no auto-submission) plus a genuinely rigorous canopy-health evidence methodology (NDVI satellite analysis, baseline/control-area comparison, GPS-tagged repeatable ground photography), framed as the first deployment of a future 'SEE' (Spatial Evidence Engine) capability. That spatial-evidence layer does not exist yet in MAYHEM and is out of scope for this case until it does.

Extracted and read eight operator-supplied docx documents. Fixed a real bug in the extraction script during this pass: the <w:t> text-run regex was also matching <w:top> (Word's paragraph-border element), corrupting every bulleted paragraph in documents that used list-item borders. Re-extracted all eight files after the fix; verified no remaining XML leakage before reading.

Independently fetched the Macleay Argus's direct coverage of the 20 May 2025 council meeting and searched specifically for the Hardened Submission Package's resolution numbers (2025.79, 2025.80) and 9/0 vote claim. Found corroboration for the softer account (declined on budget, hoped to revisit October) in the Macleay Argus and in a search-snippet of council's own May meeting wrap (a Notice of Motion for 'more information' did pass). Found no corroboration anywhere for the specific resolution numbers or vote count. Council's own site and web.archive.org both blocked automated fetch of the primary signed minutes - this remains genuinely unresolved, not disproven, and is logged as CTR-0001 / Q-0001 rather than decided either way.

Operator relayed new research: an unanimous May 2025 resolution to investigate and report back, a June 2026 report of severe ongoing camp impacts, Council's current 'historic' classification of Bellbrook, and an absence-of-substantive-intervention finding. Ran six searches and two direct-fetch attempts (both blocked, HTTP 403) before asking for citations. Found one genuinely new source independently: Council's own 27 October 2021 page confirming the colony left Bellbrook that year - a real, previously-unregistered event that offers a plausible non-sinister explanation for the 'historic' classification. Also found a partial, indirect corroboration of the 'historic' label via an unrelated Hansard-search summary that quoted Council's own page. Could not locate the June 2026 report anywhere searched. Asked operator directly for the specific citation before treating it as fact - consistent with this case's standing discipline (DEC-0002, DEC-0003) of not merging asserted-but-unconfirmed claims into the record.

Operator pasted a full ABC News article on rising North Queensland flying-fox bite/scratch exposures and Australian bat lyssavirus (ABLV) risk, flagged explicitly as relevant background rather than a Bellbrook source. Confirmed the canonical URL via search. While searching, independently found a directly on-point NSW source: Mid North Coast Local Health District's own general lyssavirus guidance - fetched and read in full. This is the same health authority EV-0004 already records council as having corresponded with regarding Bellbrook, though the content of that correspondence is still unknown. Both added as a second, distinct health-risk pathway alongside the existing droppings/histoplasmosis material (EV-0008) - bite/scratch transmission, not droppings contamination. Neither claims a confirmed Bellbrook case.

Operator pasted a real email exchange: their own 18 June 2026 notification to DCCEEW Species Policy requesting the Bellbrook camp be surveyed and registered, cc Paul Hodgson, and DCCEEW's reply (Sam Horton, Senior Policy Officer). Operator confirmed directly that this was a deliberate registration attempt made after learning any member of the public could submit one, and that it did not succeed. The reply's substantive content is significant: the National Flying Fox Monitoring Program has had no operating capacity since 2022 (paused for funding reasons), independent of anything Kempsey Shire Council has or hasn't done - a new, Commonwealth-level structural finding distinct from the case's existing council-level and state-grant-funding threads. Recorded at this repository's standard Requires Verification/Unverified classification, consistent with every other item in this case, notwithstanding the email's official appearance. Cross-referenced into DFAPTI-TA-FF-2026-00001, where the same program's status bears directly on that case's own camp-registration remedy demands.

Operator: "freeze evidence register and proceed gate snapshot." Asked the operator to confirm scope given two live open contradictions and eleven open questions - gate snapshot only (DFAPTA + SHM Gate), or the full Stages 2-6 pipeline DFAPTI-MNC-2026-00001 got from the same command form. Operator: "all gates like always. dont change the rules." Freezing at EV-0001-EV-0023 as Cycle 1's boundary (DEC-0006) and beginning Stages 2-6: DFAPTA, SHM Gate, Lattice Atlas, Temporal Projection Integrity Engine, Enforcement Notice, Advocacy Package - cloning each stage's exact mechanism from existing cases rather than inventing new page styles, per this repository's established rule. Both CTR-0001 and CTR-0002 remain genuinely Open at this freeze point and must be carried forward as unresolved through every downstream stage, not narrated toward resolution.

Operator: "not done correctly, run DFAPTA NOW" - the nine-path DFAPTA published under DEC-0006 was rejected. Asked what specifically was wrong; operator: "we will continue to do passes until I state freeze", then: "remove all the gates that are now broken because of failure to perform DFAPTA - Deep Forensic All Paths Taken Analysis. 9 paths are not all paths, the word generic is an alarm bell." This corrects a misunderstanding carried since DEC-0006: DFAPTA is an iterative, multi-pass process the operator freezes explicitly, not a single-shot synthesis produced immediately after the evidence-register freeze. Removed SHM Gate, Lattice Atlas, TPIE, Enforcement Notice and Advocacy Package (DEC-0007) since all five were built on that insufficient pass. Rebuilding DFAPTA now as Pass 1 of an explicitly ongoing process - not claiming completeness, not claiming Frozen status, and not treating "generic" synthesis as acceptable where the actual evidence supports something more specific.

Operator: "proceed DFAPTA" - ran DFAPTA Pass 2. Rather than re-reading evidence_register.json's own summaries again, extracted and read all eight preserved primary-source docx documents (cases/DFAPTI-BB-FF-2026-00001/preserved/*.docx) directly in full. This surfaced real granularity Pass 1 had missed: a seven-category community harm catalogue and a seven-item institutional-silence enumeration inside the harm-accountability document (AR-027, AR-028); the Hardened Submission Package's full procedural detail on the defeated 2/7 amendment, the SafeWork NSW/WHS Act theory, and a 30-metre buffer figure (AR-025, AR-029, AR-032); a sixth advocacy channel to Senator Mehreen Faruqi not previously logged (AR-033); and three genuine internal inconsistencies in the case's own frozen source material - an advocate name discrepancy ('Paul Hodgson' vs 'Paul Hodgkinson', AR-023), a three-way discrepancy over the colony's actual continuity (AR-024), and a direct contradiction between the media pitch's claim that submissions 'have now been lodged' and the same submissions' unsigned template state (AR-034). Added 14 new paths (AR-023 through AR-036, total now 36) and 3 new cross-path observations. None of this is new evidence - every fact cited already exists inside documents this case's register already links to; DFAPTA reads them more closely, it does not fetch anything new. Status remains "In Progress — Pass 2", not Frozen.

Operator: "I discovered something that belongs only in the advocacy package but it has been run through analysis gate. that means it hasn't followed protocol." Audited all 36 Pass 2 paths for stage-boundary violations rather than asking the operator to name the exact one - found three: AR-029 (SafeWork NSW/WHS Act remedy framework, naming specific notices to seek), AR-030 (Office of Local Government NSW submission, naming a remedy sought), and AR-033 (Senator Faruqi channel, framed around what to ask her to raise). All three were lifted from the Hardened Submission Package's own 'Submission Frameworks' section and describe remedies/recipients/asks - Advocacy Package territory, not analysis of what the evidence shows. Removed all three (DEC-0008), fixed every cross-path observation and overreach-control line referencing them, left the ID gap unclosed for traceability. DFAPTA now at 33 paths. The underlying facts remain in the preserved source material for a future Enforcement Notice/Advocacy Package build, not reintroduced here.

Operator: "ar 23 states that you did not correct a spelling mistake and instead imbedded it into the case. verification would have removed it already." Correct: AR-023 hedged 'Paul Hodgkinson' (one document) against 'Paul Hodgson' (five documents, including an independently-fetched press source and the operator's own sent email) as if it could be a genuinely distinct person, rather than recognising it as a transcription artefact. This inverts the lesson from DEC-0008 in a different direction - not merging distinct claims into a generic finding, but elevating a trivial, already-resolvable variant to the same evidentiary weight as genuine discrepancies (AR-024, AR-034). Removed AR-023 (DEC-0009), fixed CPO-008 and the overreach controls that referenced it. DFAPTA now at 32 paths. Lesson for future passes: before treating a naming/spelling variant as a discrepancy worth its own path, check whether the balance of sources already resolves it - if so, note it in passing (or correct it), don't build a hedge around it.

Operator: "it appears have been allowed into DFAPTI, a critical error on your behalf." Checked - this refines NOTE-0011's diagnosis and makes it more serious. source_register.json's SRC-0006 entry (the Hardened Submission Package's own source record, logged 2026-08-22 at case creation, well before today's DFAPTA work) already states: "Also spells the community representative's surname 'Hodgkinson,' inconsistent with 'Hodgson' used in every other document and in SRC-0001." DFAPTI had already correctly resolved this three days before AR-023 existed - a plain observation, not a hedge about a possibly-different person. The actual failure was not recognising a spelling variant in isolation - it was building DFAPTA Pass 2 without cross-checking source_register.json, so a fact DFAPTI's own frozen record already settled got re-litigated as an open discrepancy. Checked whether the same gap affected AR-024 (colony continuity) or AR-034 (lodgement contradiction) - source_register.json contains no prior mention of either, so both remain genuinely new findings, not duplicates of existing DFAPTI content. Lesson: DFAPTA must read the whole frozen DFAPTI record (source_register.json included, not just evidence_register.json) before treating anything as newly discovered.

Automated DFAPTA pass (scripts/automated-dfapta-prompt.md). Confirmed status was 'In Progress — Pass 2' before proceeding. Read decisions.json, investigation_notes.json, automation_log.json and source_register.json in full first, as the routine requires - source_register.json contains no prior mention of either finding below, so both are genuinely new, not re-litigations. Computed evidence-anchor coverage: all 23 evidence items already have at least one AR- anchor, so re-read the eight preserved primary-source documents directly for granularity rather than an uncovered EV- item, concentrating on sections Pass 2's paths had anchored but not fully quoted. Found: (1) the Community Harm and Accountability Record's own 'Evidence Base' line claims 'Kempsey Shire Council confirmed minutes 2022–2026', and the Media Pitch's 'What Is Available' section separately offers 'confirmed meeting minutes' to media - both claims sit in tension with this case's own DR-001/CTR-0001, which record that the signed confirmed minutes were never independently obtained across seven runs; (2) the same Harm and Accountability Record's governance timeline states Bellbrook was 'assessed as not feasible for vegetation management' in July 2022, a specific claim absent from every other document in this case, including the plain-language fact sheet drawn from overlapping material. Added as AR-037 and AR-038, plus CPO-010 naming this as a third instance (after AR-006, AR-034) of the same claims-vs-record gap pattern. Neither finding proposes a remedy, names a recipient, or resolves which side of either tension is accurate - both boundaries recommend a future DFAPTI pass ask the operator directly. Recursive-audit check: no other public-facing page names this case's specific pass number or path count, so no further correction was needed outside dfapta/analysis.json, dfapta/index.html and the case's own index.html.

Automated DFAPTA pass (scripts/automated-dfapta-prompt.md). Confirmed status was 'In Progress — Pass 3' before proceeding. Read decisions.json, investigation_notes.json, automation_log.json and source_register.json in full first, as the routine requires. Computed evidence-anchor coverage: all 23 evidence items already have at least one AR- anchor, so computed thread-level coverage instead (mapping each of this case's eight threads' supporting evidence to the AR- paths touching it) - THR-04 (Level 1/2 management actions vs. legal-protection framing) had the fewest paths (2) of any thread, so its underlying primary-source material was re-read directly rather than a topic chosen from a summary label. Re-read the Hardened Submission Package's Part 4 and the Community Harm and Accountability Record's Sections 2, 4 and 7 against each other and against AR-012/AR-032's existing text. Found: both documents' earlier framing (Level 1/Level 2 actions pre-approved, available independent of any Camp Management Plan) sits in tension with the Harm and Accountability Record's own later sections, which describe the Plan as the 'gateway' authorising those same Level 1/Level 2 actions - a tension that recurs inside that single document, not only between the two documents. Checked against source_register.json first: neither SRC-0006's nor SRC-0007's entry records this tension, so it is genuinely new, not a re-litigation. Added as AR-039, plus CPO-011 naming the tension it creates with AR-012/AR-032, and extended DR-004 so a future Code of Practice check resolves both questions together. Does not propose a remedy, name a recipient, or resolve which framing is accurate - the boundary recommends the primary Code of Practice text itself as the only source that could settle it. Recursive-audit check: reviewed the case's own index.html, dfapta/index.html, and the remaining un-mined text of the Ombudsman complaint, council-submission letter, and Greens senator letter for the same claims-vs-record/framing-tension pattern (CPO-006 through CPO-010) - the three letters are largely remedy/submission-ask content already outside DFAPTA's scope under DEC-0008, and their embedded factual claims are already captured by existing evidence and paths; no further correction was needed.

Automated DFAPTA pass (scripts/automated-dfapta-prompt.md). Confirmed status was 'In Progress — Pass 4' before proceeding. Read decisions.json, investigation_notes.json, automation_log.json and source_register.json in full first, as the routine requires. Computed thread-level coverage: THR-05 and THR-08 were newly tied as this case's thinnest threads (3 paths each). THR-08 has no preserved primary-source document behind it (two pasted emails only), so re-read THR-05's preserved document (the droppings-info briefing) first - already substantially mined by AR-019, with only procedural precaution advice remaining, not an evidentiary claim. Broadened to the Community Harm and Accountability Record's Section 1/governance timeline and the Media Pitch. Found: the November 2019 Black Summer bushfire-origin claim is corroborated across two independently-purposed documents for its timing, but the 'only unburnt area of the community' refuge detail recurs only within one document (twice, within its own Section 1 and governance timeline) - not independently corroborated. Also found this case's own chronology.json entry for the origin event (CHR-0001) cites EV-0001 as supporting evidence, but EV-0001 is about the 20 May 2025 meeting, not the November 2019 origin - no evidence item currently anchors the bushfire-origin claim itself. Checked against source_register.json first: neither SRC-0007's nor SRC-0010's entry records this detail or the citation gap, so it is genuinely new. Added as AR-040. Does not correct chronology.json or mint a new evidence item - both logged as candidate future-DFAPTI work in AR-040's own boundary. Recursive-audit check: spot-checked all other twelve chronology.json entries for the same citation-mismatch pattern - none found, CHR-0001 is an isolated instance. Also swept the case's own index.html, dfapta/index.html, and every other repository page referencing this case for stale pass-number/path-count framing - none found beyond the two files this pass updates.

Automated DFAPTA pass (scripts/automated-dfapta-prompt.md). Confirmed status was 'In Progress — Pass 5' before proceeding. Read decisions.json, investigation_notes.json, automation_log.json and source_register.json in full first, as the routine requires. Computed thread-level coverage: THR-04, THR-05 and THR-08 remained tied as this case's thinnest threads (3 paths each), with THR-05 and THR-08 already exhausted of unmined primary-source content by Pass 5. Re-read AR-039's own boundary, which had deliberately scoped itself to the Level 1/Level 2 pre-approval claim and named four other items on the Community Harm and Accountability Record's Section 2 list it did not examine: infrastructure hardening, resident subsidies, school support, formal advocacy. Re-read Section 2 against the same document's Section 3, Section 4 and Section 5 for the first of those, infrastructure hardening. Found: Section 2 lists infrastructure hardening as available to council regardless of the species-protection constraint, the same way it lists Level 1/2 actions - but Section 4's own funding-mechanism analysis (EV-0011) and Section 5's advocacy-chain summary (EV-0004) show the only funding pathway this document describes for hardening works, external grants, is itself plan-gated, and Bellbrook has no plan (EV-0002). Checked against source_register.json first: neither SRC-0007's nor SRC-0005's entry records this connection, so it is genuinely new - an extension of CPO-011's existing pattern to a second action category, not a re-litigation. Added as AR-041, plus a corresponding overreach-control line, and extended DR-003's request text so a future grants-program-guidelines check resolves both AR-002's and this path's question together. Recursive-audit check: checked whether the same pattern recurs for the two remaining unexamined Section 2 items (resident subsidies, formal advocacy) - the source material supplies no comparable funding-mechanism or authorisation detail for either, so no further extension is currently supportable; also checked school support specifically (already delivered per Section 5) and found no plan-dependency claimed for it, so that item's framing is not contradicted the same way. Also swept the case's own index.html, dfapta/index.html, and every other repository page referencing this case for stale pass-number/path-count framing - none found beyond the two files this pass updates.

Automated DFAPTA pass (scripts/automated-dfapta-prompt.md). Confirmed status was 'In Progress — Pass 6' before proceeding. Read decisions.json, investigation_notes.json, automation_log.json and source_register.json in full first, as the routine requires. Computed thread-level coverage: THR-04, THR-05 and THR-08 remained tied as this case's thinnest threads (3 paths each), with THR-04 and THR-05 already characterised as exhausted of unmined primary-source content. Re-read in full, rather than trusting the prior summary, the three preserved documents (council-submission letter, Ombudsman complaint, Greens senator letter) DEC-0012/DEC-0013 had described only as remedy/submission-ask content - confirmed that characterisation held. Noticed a candidate discrepancy while reading them: the council-submission letter states 'five and a half years' of harm at the May 2025 decision point, while the Ombudsman complaint and senator letter state 'six and a half years'. Checked this against the Community Harm and Accountability Record (EV-0004) before treating it as a finding, and found the source document itself uses both figures correctly for two different reference points (time elapsed at the May 2025 decision vs. time elapsed as of each document's own June 2026 drafting date) - not a genuine inconsistency, so nothing was added for it. This is exactly the kind of near-miss DEC-0009 warns against manufacturing in the other direction: a difference that looks like a discrepancy until checked against its own source context. Found the actual new finding in EV-0022's own record instead: the operator's 18 June 2026 email to DCCEEW states no formal species identification, ecological assessment, or census of the Bellbrook colony has ever been conducted by council, CSIRO or any government agency since November 2019 - sharper than AR-015's existing 'no data in this case's own register' finding. Checked against source_register.json first: SRC-0019's entry does not record this specific claim, so it is genuinely new. Added as AR-042. Does not allege any agency concealed an existing assessment - reports only the operator's own sourced claim that none is known to exist. Recursive-audit check: having just caught myself almost over-reading the five/six-and-a-half-years figures as a discrepancy, checked whether any other repeated duration or count figure in this case's documents shows the same near-miss pattern - none did. Also swept the case's own index.html, dfapta/index.html, and every other repository page referencing this case for stale pass-number/path-count framing - none found beyond the two files this pass updates.

Automated DFAPTA pass (scripts/automated-dfapta-prompt.md). Confirmed status was 'In Progress — Pass 7' before proceeding. Read decisions.json, investigation_notes.json, automation_log.json and source_register.json in full first, as the routine requires. Before starting the case work, found this session's git HEAD detached with five unpushed commits spanning this case's own prior two passes and DFAPTI-MNC-2026-00001's most recent three - fast-forwarded `main` onto them and pushed, since origin was a strict ancestor and nothing was discarded. Computed thread-level coverage: THR-04 and THR-05 remained tied as this case's thinnest threads (3 paths each), with THR-08 now ahead at 4. Re-read the Hardened Submission Package's Part 4 and the droppings-info briefing in full again rather than accepting the prior passes' 'exhausted' characterisation on trust - both confirmed exhausted. Re-read the council-submission letter and Ombudsman complaint (already re-read in full by Pass 7 for a different purpose) and found both treat the absence of any disclosed output from the August/September 2025 community consultation as a distinct undisclosed item - not covered by AR-028's existing seven-item enumeration, which concerns only silences from external bodies, not silence toward the community that generated the consultation material itself. Checked against source_register.json first: neither SRC-0008's nor SRC-0011's entry records this specific claim, so it is genuinely new. Added as AR-043. Does not allege the consultation output was deliberately withheld, and does not propose that council be asked to produce it - that is Enforcement Notice/Advocacy Package territory (DEC-0008). Recursive-audit check: after the fast-forward and push, re-verified git status was clean with nothing stranded; also swept the case's own index.html, dfapta/index.html, and every other repository page referencing this case for stale pass-number/path-count framing - none found beyond the two files this pass updates.

Automated DFAPTA pass (scripts/automated-dfapta-prompt.md). Confirmed status was 'In Progress — Pass 8' before proceeding. Read decisions.json, investigation_notes.json, automation_log.json and source_register.json in full first, as the routine requires. Verified origin/main was a strict ancestor, fast-forwarded `main` onto the detached HEAD, and pushed, recovering all seven commits. Computed thread-level coverage: THR-04 and THR-05 remained tied as this case's thinnest threads (3 paths each). Re-read the Hardened Submission Package's Part 4 and the droppings-info briefing a fourth time rather than trusting four prior passes' 'exhausted' characterisation - both again confirmed exhausted. Checked against source_register.json first: neither SRC-0007's nor SRC-0005's entry records this specific framing, so it is genuinely new. Added as AR-044. Does not allege the non-reversal reflects deliberate obstruction or any other motive - both documents state it as a governance-record fact. Recursive-audit check: after the fast-forward/push, re-verified git status was clean with nothing stranded; checked whether the same 'explicitly noted as unreversed' framing recurs for any other decision point (the October 2025 non-appearance, the March 2026 letter's grant intentions) - neither is framed as a 'reversible' decision by any source document, so no further extension is currently supportable. Also swept the case's own index.html, dfapta/index.html, and every other repository page referencing this case for stale pass-number/path-count framing - none found beyond the two files this pass updates.

Read decisions.json, investigation_notes.json, automation_log.json and source_register.json in full first, as the routine requires. Before starting case work, found this session's git HEAD detached again with nine unpushed commits (this case's own most recent pass plus DFAPTI-MNC-2026-00001's two most recent passes) - a third occurrence of the failure mode DEC-0016 and DEC-0017 already recorded. Verified origin/main was a strict ancestor, fast-forwarded `main` onto the detached HEAD, and pushed, recovering all nine commits. Independently re-read the Hardened Submission Package's Part 4 and the Community Harm and Accountability Record's Sections 2, 4, 5 and 7 rather than trusting five prior passes' 'exhausted' characterisation - confirmed exhausted, and confirmed the two Section 2 items Pass 6 had already found unsupportable (resident subsidies, formal advocacy) still carry no comparable funding/authorisation detail. Turned to the council-submission letter (EV-0006) and found its own six-named-recipient 'submitted simultaneously' claim - already shown by AR-034 to assert completed lodgement against unsigned templates - has a second, independent gap: this case's material contains a matching drafted document for only two of the six named recipients (council itself, the NSW Ombudsman); the one further draft that exists (the Greens senator letter) targets a recipient outside the named six. Recursive-audit check: after the fast-forward/push, re-verified git status was clean with nothing stranded; checked whether the same 'named recipient with no matching draft' pattern recurs for any other multi-recipient claim in this case's material - the only other one (the March 2026 letter's advocacy-chain list) names entities council itself corresponded with, not a submission this case drafted, so it does not transfer. Automated DFAPTA pass (scripts/automated-dfapta-prompt.md). Confirmed status was 'In Progress — Pass 10' before proceeding. Read decisions.json, investigation_notes.json, automation_log.json and source_register.json in full first, as the routine requires. Git was already clean and up to date on main at the start of this run - no stranded commits to recover this time. Computed thread-level coverage: THR-04 and THR-05 remained tied as this case's thinnest threads (3 paths each). Re-read the Hardened Submission Package's Part 4 and the droppings-info briefing directly rather than trusting six prior passes' 'exhausted' characterisation - both again confirmed exhausted; the droppings briefing's undiagnosed-infection-rate reasoning is already fully captured by AR-019. Re-read all eight preserved primary-source documents in full instead of narrowing straight to the two thinnest threads' own material. Found: the council-submission letter, the NSW Ombudsman complaint, and the Greens senator letter each independently cite an attachment titled 'Bellbrook Flying Fox — Community Harm and Accountability Record, June 2026', while the record itself states its own preparation date as 'May 2026' - the same month this case's own source register already uses for it. The mismatch recurs identically across all three independently-addressed drafts, not as an isolated typo. Checked against source_register.json first: none of SRC-0006's, SRC-0007's, SRC-0008's, SRC-0009's or SRC-0011's entries records this specific date discrepancy, so it is genuinely new. Added as AR-046. Does not determine which date is accurate, and does not allege the mismatch was deliberate - the likelier explanation is all three June-dated letters were drafted from a template restating each letter's own month rather than checking the attachment's actual title. Recursive-audit check: checked whether the same self-dating-vs-citation mismatch recurs for any other dated document in this case (the 18 March 2026 council letter, the 20 May 2025 meeting date, the 18 June 2026 DCCEEW email) - all are cited consistently with their own stated dates everywhere referenced; this is currently an isolated instance. Also swept the case's own index.html, dfapta/index.html, and every other repository page referencing this case for stale pass-number/path-count framing - none found beyond the two files this pass updates.
